newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S GONCZ SIGNS BILL HE EARLIER VETOED.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S GONCZ SIGNS BILL HE EARLIER VETOED.

text.p: Hungarian President Arpad Goncz has signed into law two bills he vetoed in January despite the fact that one was returned to him unchanged.
Goncz will inform Parliament of his decision on Tuesday, the Hungarian daily Nepszabadsag reported.

Goncz shocked the governing coalition of Socialists and Free Democrats in January by vetoing a conflict of interest bill which bans MPs from holding positions in companies with a state-owned stake of over 10 percent.
He rejected the bill on the grounds that it applied only to posts taken up since the 1994 elections.
He also sent back a set of amendments to the privatisation law which would allow the state privatisation agency APV to transfer assets free of charge to municipalities and state-owned cooperatives.
The privatisation amendments had been fiercely attacked by opposition parties on the grounds that such powers would be tantamount to "legalised corruption".
The government returned the bill to Goncz with the clause on cooperatives removed.
However, the conflict of interest bill was returned unchanged and under Hungary's constitution Goncz is obliged to sign it as it was passed by a two-thirds majority.

Any Hungarian citizen, including opposition MPs, will still be entitled to challenge the law before the Constitutional Court but parliamentary leader of the opposition Fidesz party said they would not do so.
"This is not a constitutional question," Joszef Szajer told Reuters. "We will push for a stricter law at a later date."
